question.problem: Mary is randomly picking a candy from a bag and putting it back in until she gets a lemon-flavored candy. Approximately, $6%$ of the candies in the bag are lemon-flavored. What is the probability that the $9$th candy is the first lemon-flavored candy picked? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.

current_example.problem: An archer is practicing archery. On average, the archer has a $7\%$ chance of missing every shot he makes. What is the probability that the archer will miss for the first time on the $8$th shot? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
current_example.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x) = (1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of shots until the archer misses. Since the chance of missing each shot is $7\%,$ the number of shots  until the archer misses can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p = 7\% = \dfrac{7}{100} = 0.07.
$$

So, $X\sim\textrm{Geom}(0.07).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.07)^{x-1}(0.07) \\  & =(0.93)^{x-1}(0.07)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the archer will miss for the first time on the $8$th shot is 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=8) & =f(8) \\  & =(0.93)^{8-1}(0.07) \\  & =(0.93)^{7}(0.07) \\  & ≈0.042\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
